, for model checking and satisfability, the complexity of hybrid logics over equivalence relations is in general between NP and NExpTime, with some cases being polynomial-time solvable and some being complete for PSPACE and N2ExpTime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expressive power of a hybrid language is not a good indicator for the complexity of the satisfiability problem, while it is an indicator for the complexity for model checking.
, in the absence of atomic propositions, the complexity of model checking is always PSPACE-complete, whereas the complexity of satisfiability depends on the language and the frame type.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of these problems can vary dramatically depending on the combination of operators and the presence of atomic propositions and complete frames.
